text:
Florida spent most of the night playing a different game than the one the scoreboard showed for two periods. VAN led 2-0 after the first despite being outchanced 2.13 to 0.76 in expected goals, with Liam Ohgren and Elias Pettersson each finishing snap shots on modest looks (12 and 19 percent). Leevi Meriläinen kept it there, stopping Anton Lundell on a 22 percent chance and finishing 0.93 goals better than the 39 shots he faced deserved.

Brady Tkachuk eventually broke through. His first goal, at 11:11 of the third, came on a 2 percent chance, the least likely of the night. With the goalie presumably pulled, he tied it at 19:47 with a slap shot, then won it 2:23 into overtime with a snap shot, Seth Jones and Sam Reinhart assisting. That made three goals on six shots for Tkachuk, and Jones, who logged 26:18, picked up two assists.

The underlying numbers say the comeback was earned. FLA finished with 3.93 expected goals to 2.45 for VAN, a 72-41 edge in shot attempts, and a 74 percent chance of winning in simulated replays of every shot. VAN did hold Florida to 3.17 expected goals at even strength against its own 1.56, but the gap stayed wide. Akira Schmid faced only 17 shots and allowed two, while Meriläinen did the heavy lifting at the other end. A 2-0 lead built on two efficient finishes was never going to survive that volume.
